findings.problem: The candidate places the completed office traversal and doorway crossing, the subsequent hallway-to-room transition, and the distinct final circular-table approach in one undifferentiated stage. These are separate source-supported navigation objectives with completed transition outcomes; keeping all of them in one phase buries the later room-entry and target-selection focus.

teaching_notes.decision_reason: All source requirements are preserved, but the candidate collapses multiple completed transitions and a later independent target approach into one broad stage.
teaching_notes.transfer_rule: A material under-segmentation finding requires a completed earlier objective, a distinct later objective, a supported handoff, and concrete loss of local focus. Cite the actual source and candidate evidence; do not rely on instruction length or verb count.
teaching_notes.anti_pattern: Do not force splits at every clause or room reference. A single continuous maneuver with no independently supported intermediate completion remains one stage.
teaching_notes.why_this_review_matters: This is a grouping defect rather than a source-fidelity omission: the words remain, but the stage organization obscures distinct local navigation focus.
